title: Comparison of Dual Task Gait Characteristics in Individuals With Amputation and Healty Individuals
brief_summary: In amputee, dual task has been found to cause a decrease in walking speed. However, there is no study of how gait characteristics are affected when the speed does not change. The aim of this study is to compare the time-distance characteristics of walking with single task, cognitive dual task, motor dual task in transtibial, transfemoral amputee and healthy people.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Using a transtibial or transfemoral prosthesis for at least 1 year,
* Between the ages of 18-65,

Exclusion Criteria:

* To be diagnosed as a neurological, orthopedic, cognitive disorder,
* Having a condition other than amputation that may affect gait.
* Having different permanent disabilities other than amputation,
* Using walking aid,
study_population: Transtibial amputees, Transfemoral amputees, Healty individuals
